clue.text: Evil genius regularly cooled off in the embrace of a Spice Girl

indicators.note: being in someone's embrace means being held inside their arms, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Ginger Spice, Geri Halliwell, was one of the Spice Girls

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A scheming mastermind cools down in the arms of one of the Spice Girls.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'cooled off' sit inside GINGER after its G, giving GOLDFINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric Goldfinger is the criminal mastermind villain of Ian Fleming's James Bond novel and film.

clue.text: Golf — a miserable, vacuous pastime

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its inner letters and only its ends remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A grumble that golf is a dreary, empty way to spend time.
explanation.definitionFit: A game is any activity played for amusement, which is what a pastime is.

clue.text: Callas playing Aida finally here?

indicators.note: players perform a piece in their own way, so these letters are performed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written: Maria Callas, the opera singer

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of the opera's name

explanation.surface: Maria Callas singing Verdi's Aida: where might that take place?
explanation.walkthrough: 'here?' is the definition: a place where Callas might sing Aida, the question mark marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala is the celebrated Milan opera house where Callas often sang, a likely venue for such a performance.

clue.text: Honest, intense, moving work by Shelley

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position and land in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: frank means candid, honest
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A review praising one of Shelley's works as truthful, powerful and emotionally affecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' reads as praise for the book, but it signals the rearrangement. The Shelley is Mary, not her husband Percy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankenstein is the 1818 novel written by Mary Shelley.

clue.text: Game played with cards for gold coin once

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card game, also called nap, in which players bid for tricks
second meaning: a former French twenty-franc gold piece

explanation.surface: Gambling at cards with an old gold coin as the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon names both a trick-taking card game and the old French gold coin bearing the emperor's head.

clue.text: Trouble on line that might have a global impact?

definitions.text: that might have a global impact?

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fault on a communications line that could have worldwide consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble on line' sounds like a phone fault, but the first word stirs up the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is a periodic warming of the Pacific Ocean that disrupts weather patterns around the world.

clue.text: Young bear munching tail of fresh fish

indicators.note: something munching food holds it in its mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cub is a young bear

indicators.note: an animal's tail is at its back end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A bear cub eating the end of a freshly caught fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh fish' looks like a phrase, but 'fresh' supplies a letter and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Tough to accept extra official here in Cambridge

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: hard means tough
VAR, the video assistant referee, is an additional match official in football

explanation.surface: A rigid institution in Cambridge struggling to take on another administrator.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge suggests the English university, but this is Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard University is located in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Codswallop, tosh sad Red Labourite pens when upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something tips it over so it reads from bottom to top
to pen is to enclose, so the run of words holds the solution within it

parts.note: the letters running from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on what a gloomy left-wing Labour writer produces when angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tosh' looks like a second definition beside Codswallop, but it is part of the string that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop and balderdash are both informal British words for senseless talk or nonsense.

clue.text: More canapés prepared without European cheese

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so these letters are reworked into a new order
without means lacking, so the named letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Extra party nibbles made up without any continental cheese on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft, creamy Italian cheese, used in tiramisu.

clue.text: Test alloy of gold and aluminium

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A lab test on a metal mixture of gold and aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alloy of' fits the metallurgy picture but just joins the two metals.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a kind of test.

clue.text: The part of a plant where reproduction takes place?

definitions.text: The part of a plant where reproduction takes place?

parts.words: The part of a plant where reproduction takes place?
parts.note: surface reading: the flower or organ of a living plant where it breeds; setter's reading: the part of a factory where identical copies of a product are turned out

explanation.walkthrough: Plant and reproduction both suggest botany; here a plant is a factory and reproduction is making copies of a product.
explanation.definitionFit: On a factory's production line, workers or machines put together the same item over and over.

clue.text: Prohibit Kenya's premier financial institution

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit

indicators.note: premier means first in rank, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: Kenya's prime minister outlawing a lender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kenya's premier' wants to be the country's prime minister, but it means only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a business that holds deposits and lends money, so it is a financial institution.

clue.text: Captures head, but not in portrait

parts.note: lands, as in lands a fish, means captures
a cape or headland is a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Photography talk: a camera captures a head, but not in portrait format.
explanation.walkthrough: Portrait and landscape are the two page or screen orientations, upright and sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape layout is the wide, horizontal orientation, the alternative to the tall portrait format.

clue.text: One tossed Charlie aside supported by Donald and Ian — a Scot

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so what follows is placed below
putting something aside sets it apart, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a caber is the long pole tossed at Highland games
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Don is short for Donald
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thrown aside, with Donald and Ian holding them up, all Scots together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One tossed' is not a person: caber tossing is a Highland games event, a fitting thing to find in a Scottish clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdonian is a native or inhabitant of Aberdeen, a city in Scotland.

clue.text: Mensa member packed underwear

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
something packed is in a box

explanation.surface: A member of the high-IQ society has packed some underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order is reversed: the underwear comes first in the answer, followed by 'in box'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is an informal word for a very clever person, the kind who might join the high-IQ society Mensa.

clue.text: First edition that might have been given a four-star rating?

definitions.text: that might have been given a four-star rating?

parts.note: to be in the lead is to be first
ed. is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A collectible first edition that a reviewer would have rated four stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The four stars are not a critic's: in Britain leaded petrol was sold as four-star.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-star was the British grade name for leaded petrol, so leaded fuel carried that rating.

clue.text: Musical dance that's produced by Tom?

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A musical dance number put on by someone called Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a person's name, but a tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats cough up hairballs of swallowed fur, so a tomcat might produce one.

clue.text: Distant meteor exploded

indicators.note: something that has exploded is blown apart, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A far-off meteor burst apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote and distant are synonyms for far away.

clue.text: Mum can put on extremely exclusive daytime show

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is put on something sits above it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Mother is able to stage a very select show in the daytime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or film.

clue.text: Airline boards excited sunseekers jetting off here

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and stirred about, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: BA is British Airways
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Eager holidaymakers board a plane bound for the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boards' reads as a verb for getting on the plane; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a sunny Caribbean island, a popular destination for holidaymakers flying in.

clue.text: Sleeping dung-beetle chap touched at the front

parts.note: a dor is a kind of dung beetle
a chap is a man

indicators.note: the front of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A fellow resting beside a dung beetle, gently tapped at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: DOR is an old name for the dung beetle, rarely seen outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or asleep, as a hibernating animal is.

clue.text: Measure of power flipped in old American capital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the word reads the other way round

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power

explanation.surface: A unit of power turned upside down in a former American capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old American capital' reads as one phrase, but 'old' and 'American' are the outer letters and 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Oh, you loudly giggle about fine clothier

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the two words said out sound like the letters O and U

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to titter is to giggle
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone teasing a tailor by giggling about how fine he is.
explanation.walkthrough: TITTER goes round F after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothes and equipment, so is a clothier.

clue.text: Reversed wagon three feet

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A wagon backing up a short distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is an imperial length equal to three feet.

clue.text: Island broadcaster using radio

indicators.note: radio is heard and not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: An island's broadcaster sending out programmes over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a TV broadcaster, which is why the clue specifies radio for the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Bars popular Poles

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Pubs that are well liked by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; it means the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are pubs, places where drinks are served at a bar.

clue.text: After knocking back Rafa's IPA, Rick drained Pride here?

indicators.note: knocking back a drink tips it up, so this word is read from end to start
after places the remaining pieces behind the first one

parts.note: the name with its S, read backwards
taken as written: India pale ale

indicators.note: a drained word has its contents emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Rafa downs his pale ale and Rick finishes his, in a scene at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A pride is a group of lions, which visitors drive past in a safari park.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions are kept in safari parks, so a pride might be found living there.

clue.text: November over, starts to enjoy later festival

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Once November has ended, a festival comes along later to be enjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the winter festival.

clue.text: California 50¢ note? Phone bank

parts.note: Cal. is the abbreviation for California
L is the Roman numeral for 50
the sign stands for a cent
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A California fifty-cent note: does it come from a telephone bank?
explanation.walkthrough: '50¢ note' looks like a banknote, but splits into a numeral, a coin and a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A call centre is an office where staff handle large volumes of phone calls, also called a phone bank.
